Can you move your website and keep your business email?

A hypothetical Varanasi fabric wholesaler checks its mailbox, domain settings and quote form before moving the website.

By SiteSutra · 28 November 2026

← All articlesYour next step ↓

You can usually keep your business email when you move your website. First confirm who runs the mailbox and whether it depends on the old hosting plan. If the mail service is independent, a website move can often be limited to the web records. If the old plan includes the mailbox or relays website notifications, keep it active until you have tested the replacement or confirmed the provider will retain the service.

The new site is ready. Can Renu cancel the old plan?

Renu runs a hypothetical fabric wholesaler in Varanasi. Retailers reply to order threads using the same address printed on her sample cards. She wants to move the catalogue website to a new host and keep those conversations and the address. On the old invoice, she sees a single hosting line. Her team also receives quote requests from a form on the old site.

She asks the provider two specific questions. Which subscription keeps the team’s mailboxes and aliases running? What service actually sends the form notification? The first answer tells her which plan to retain or migrate. The second tells her whether moving the website could interrupt new enquiries even if staff email works.

Choose the smallest move that serves the project

Renu’s checks before approving the move
What the team findsWhat to planEvidence before cancelling
Mail and DNS have independent providersAsk the developer whether the new site can use the existing DNS provider and change only the web recordsNew site and normal mail both work on the custom domain
The move includes new nameserversCompare the current DNS records with the new provider’s copy and confirm the mail related entries and their dependenciesThe new DNS answers match the approved plan and mail tests pass
Mail is part of the old hosting planConfirm a standalone mail option or schedule a mailbox migration that covers aliases and old messagesStaff can send, receive and access the history they agreed to keep
The quote form depends on the old serverConfigure and test a supported notification or submission service on the new siteA test quote arrives in the agreed inbox with the expected reply address

Check each row that applies. Renu can keep her mail provider and still need to replace the form integration. If she cannot identify the service behind a row, she marks that dependency as unresolved before approving the switch.

Ask what changes at the domain

DNS records tell services where to find the site and mail. Web hosts usually supply an address or hostname to use for the site. MX records direct incoming email. Other records can help receiving systems authenticate messages sent on behalf of the domain. Ask your provider or developer to identify the records your setup needs and document the proposed changes. A hosting provider’s instructions should give the values for your domain. Vercel’s custom domain setup.

A nameserver change hands responsibility for answering the domain’s DNS queries to another provider. Before approving one, compare the old and new record lists, including mail authentication and any hostname referenced by mail records. Cloudflare’s setup guidance calls for reviewing imported records because an automatic scan can miss entries. Cloudflare’s nameserver setup and record review.

Test the mailbox and the form independently

Before the move, send a message from an outside account to the address on your website and reply to it. Repeat with any shared aliases your team uses for orders. Record which accounts and message history staff can open. After the switch, repeat those tests and send a labelled quote through the new public form with details you control. Ask the person who handles enquiries to confirm that the same reference reached the agreed inbox and that replying goes to the intended address.

Agree on a launch window, who decides whether to revert, and which settings they would restore if a check fails. Keep the old service available through the agreed verification window. Removing the old plan is a separate decision that depends on whether mail, website notifications or retained history still rely on it.

Approve the hosting move and cancellation separately

Renu asks the developer to list the web records to change, the mail dependencies to preserve and the form notification to test. She gives her order desk the mail and quote checks. Once both have been checked and the provider confirms which services the old plan covers, she can decide whether to cancel it.
